findings.title: A confirmation timeout is treated as a stall, not as 'timeout is never a no'
findings.summary: When a risky-confirm times out, Samantha says it still needs your OK and stops, instead of moving the job forward.
findings.impact: A missed or slow approval freezes the conversation for minutes and leaves the task undone.
findings.done_when: If a confirmation times out, she does not treat that as a no. She either retries the safe work, or gives one light prompt and stays ready to continue, without a long silence.
findings.recommendation: On confirm timeout, do not tell the user the action still requires OK as if they refused. Follow the Her spec: a timeout is never a no. Complete clearly safe work, or re-ask once without stalling the turn for the full confirm window.
findings.observed: Same session 9463464a, T2, 14 Nov 2026 ~22:32-22:34 IST. After confirm_risky for echo $((17 * 19)) timed out, she replied: 'The confirmation timed out, Guru, so it still needs your OK to run.' The turn left a roughly two-minute gap (helper response_done step_ms=123696). She did not compute 323 until T2b was asked again. Her spec trait 4: 'a timeout is never a no'; 0 = stalls, or 'user said no' on a timeout.

findings.title: Skill file mixes always-needed rules with the step workflow, and the chart does not show the real flow
findings.summary: The skill file repeats the workflow in a sentence and a list, while the rules that apply at every step are missing or written as bare commands. The chart only lists which file loads, not the loop, the gate, or which scripts run.
findings.impact: An agent following the skill can miss the rules that apply at every step, load the wrong files, or treat the chart as the workflow when it is not. The skill also falls short of the usual skill-writing rules for descriptions, reasons, and behaviour tests.
findings.done_when: The skill file holds only the always-needed rules, each with a short reason, a one-row-per-step router table, and the self-check line. The description names the real situations when to use the skill. The chart is generated from the workflow definition and shows the loop, the gate exit, colours for the skill file, references and scripts, and click-to-highlight. Current and After views remain as a toggle on that flow, with a delete, simplify, optimize, automate, or keep badge on each node. Gate numbers come from the definition, not the skill file. Two or three realistic prompts are saved and compared against the previous skill. Named tests cover each of these, including the toggle and badges, the package version is raised, and the skill is installed locally.
findings.observed: Current SKILL.md in 0.1.37 is about 25 lines: a one-line workflow, a numbered list of eight steps, and a When/Load table that repeats trigger names inside the Load cells and bundles several steps on one row. Always-needed rules (orchestrator does not write fix code, Codex routing, who writes the tracker, independent groups, status accuracy, one fix total, Introspect after Verify) are not in the skill file. Gate numbers 15 and 16 are discussed in conversation, not read from workflow_definition.json (default_threshold is 15). statechart.html is a two-column Current vs After trigger list with no loop-back or scripts. No evals/evals.json exists. Guru asked for this redesign at 21:15 IST Asia/Calcutta on 17 Nov 2026, then at 21:17 IST Asia/Calcutta asked to keep Current and After as a toggle with Elon verdict badges on the nodes.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite SKILL.md to always-needed rules plus a one-row-per-step router and the self-check line; move step-only content into the matching reference file; generate a real flow chart from workflow_definition.json with Current and After as a toggle and verdict badges on the nodes; add evals and named tests; bump and install the package.

findings.title: The tracker carries every already-verified merged finding into each new list
findings.summary: When a list rolls over, every already verified and merged finding is copied into the new list, so later lists keep growing even when almost all of that history is finished.
findings.impact: Each new list is slower to read and update, and a new verification run also opens a pending check for each of those old items even though they were already finished on an earlier list.
findings.done_when: Rollover moves already merged, verified findings into an archive file and leaves only open, blocked, or still-current items on the new list. A verification run on the new list does not open pending checks for archived items.
findings.observed: On 17 Nov 2026 around 22:28-22:31 IST Asia/Calcutta, list #115 still held 82 already-verified merged findings plus the later items, for 87 findings in total. Starting the 0.1.38 verification run bcl-0.1.38-44f585be-115 created 87 checks, of which 86 stayed pending after BCL-38 was recorded fixed. Those pending checks are almost all carried items from earlier lists.
findings.recommendation: At rollover, move merged verified findings to an archive and keep only unresolved work on the new list. Do not open pending verification checks for archived items.

findings.title: Introspect records are stored as ordinary findings
findings.summary: Each Introspect save is written as a WF finding on the change list, so review notes sit in the same list as product fixes.
findings.impact: The list is harder to scan. The verified-fix count already leaves these records out, so they add clutter without changing the gate number.
findings.done_when: Introspect output is stored in the round history, not as a WF finding on the list, and earlier WF-07 through WF-21 records can be moved there without changing the gate count.
findings.observed: On 17 Nov 2026, #115 still included WF-06 through WF-21 as findings marked verified_fixed, including WF-07 through WF-21 from earlier Introspect saves. The gate count already excludes completed Introspect records.
findings.recommendation: Write Introspect into round history and stop creating WF findings for those reviews.

findings.title: Snapshot commits flood the branch
findings.summary: The live tracker already lives outside git, but almost every tracker write also creates a snapshot live tracker commit on the PR branch.
findings.impact: The branch history is mostly snapshots, which buries the real fix commits and makes review and recovery harder.
findings.done_when: The branch is snapshotted at most once per stage change, or once at rollover, and ordinary tracker writes do not each add a git commit.
findings.observed: Earlier on #115, 44 of 84 commits were snapshot live tracker. During the 17 Nov 2026 BCL-38 verify, bcl verify itself created more snapshot commits, including 6ccee3a1 after a failed verify. The live tracker is already at /Users/gurusharan/.agents/state/batched-change-list/ingpoc--agent-plugins/115.json.
findings.recommendation: Snapshot once per stage change or at rollover, not after every tracker write.

findings.title: Blocked items that need a real microphone or Windows are carried on every list
findings.summary: Four items that cannot be checked without a real microphone or a Windows machine have been copied forward on every list since #110.
findings.impact: Each new list still shows work that cannot be done on this Mac, which distracts from items that can be fixed now.
findings.done_when: OBS-23, OBS-25, BCL-13, and BCL-18 sit in a separate blocked list and are only reviewed when that hardware is available.
findings.observed: On 17 Nov 2026, #115 still carries OBS-23 and OBS-25, which need a real microphone and spoken playback, and BCL-13 and BCL-18, which need a live Windows runtime. All four have been rolled forward since #110 and remain blocked.

findings.title: Rolling over at 15 verified fixes and merging only at 16 or more can leave the earlier PR stuck
findings.summary: A list can roll over once 15 items are verified, but the previous PR can be merged only at 16 or more, so a list can close out from under a PR that still cannot merge.
findings.impact: The earlier PR can sit open, as #112 has, after work has already moved to a later list.
findings.done_when: The skill and the workflow definition either hold rollover until the merge number is also met, or they use the same number for both.
findings.observed: workflow_definition.json has gate.default_threshold 15 for report and rollover, and gate.merge_previous_pr_threshold 16 for merge. That mismatch is what left #112 stuck. The 0.1.38 redesign wired the two numbers but did not change the hold-or-equal rule. Guru's practice has been to hold rollover for one more round rather than roll over at exactly 15.
findings.recommendation: Encode holding rollover until 16 or more verified fixes, or make the rollover and merge numbers the same.

findings.title: A one-item docs or chart change still runs the full fix loop alone
findings.summary: A single documentation or chart change is still planned, installed, verified, and introspected as its own round, even when it could have shared a round with other small items.
findings.impact: Simple wording or chart work takes a full cycle, which delays the next batch of product fixes.
findings.done_when: Small, independent docs or chart items may be placed in the same Plan and fix round as other independent work, and the skill says when that is allowed.
findings.observed: Round 1 of #115 ran only BCL-38, a skill-file and chart redesign, through the full plan, Codex, Terra review, install, verify, and Introspect loop. Verify later needed two one-file follow-ups. No other open product item was included.
findings.recommendation: Allow small independent docs or chart items to share a round.

findings.title: The change-list viewer can serve the previous list's worktree and go stale during a round
findings.summary: The live page can keep running from the previous list's folder, and it can sit unchanged while a round is still in progress, so it is marked Stale.
findings.impact: A reader can look at the wrong list, or at an outdated page, and think no work is happening.
findings.done_when: The #115 viewer is always started from the #115 worktree, and the page refreshes during a round so it does not stay Stale while work is underway.
findings.observed: On 17 Nov 2026 around 21:20 IST Asia/Calcutta, the #115 page was marked Stale and was being served from the old #114 worktree folder. During the later BCL-38 verify, tracker writes updated the HTML snapshot, but the running viewer still needed a restart from the #115 worktree.
findings.recommendation: Always start or restart the current list's viewer from that list's worktree, and refresh the page during a round.

findings.title: The test suite leaves viewer processes running
findings.summary: Tests start local viewers and do not always stop them, so leftover example viewers pile up on the machine.
findings.impact: The Mac accumulates dozens of idle test servers, which wastes process slots and can confuse later viewer checks.
findings.done_when: Every test that starts a viewer stops it before the test ends, including when the test fails, and a named test proves leftover viewers are not left behind.
findings.observed: On 17 Nov 2026, about 42 leftover example--project--123 serve.py processes were first seen, with --data under /private/var/folders/.../T/. After later worktree and verify-bcl38.sh runs, 98 such test viewers were still running. Real list viewers and port 8765 were left untouched.
findings.recommendation: Tests must shut down any viewer they start, including on failure, and a named test should catch leaks.

findings.title: The page shows Stale while a round is still running
findings.summary: During round 2 the #115 page showed Stale while Codex lanes were running, because nothing writes the tracker between lane transitions, so the 10-minute no-update rule fires during long Codex jobs.
findings.impact: The owner sees Stale and the wrong lane phase (TRACKER-LEAN still Fixing after its follow-up finished) and cannot tell whether work is happening.
findings.done_when: While any lane has a live job, the page never shows Stale; each Codex job start and finish and each lane transition writes the tracker and re-renders through the bcl CLI; Stale still appears when no job is alive and nothing has updated. Proven by a named test and checked on the installed copy. Lane labels never run ahead of reality: the source suite run before push and install shows as Pre-push suite (distinct from Verify, the post-install check), and Installing appears only when bcl install starts.
findings.observed: On 18 Nov 2026 Guru saw the #115 page marked Updated 9:25 IST, Stale, with TRACKER-LEAN still Fixing although its Luna follow-up had finished; at 09:46 IST he reported Stale again. render.py marks Stale after tracking.workflow.stale_after_min (10) minutes without a workflow update even when lanes are running, and lane progress was written only by hand. At 09:47 IST the page also showed all four lanes Installing while nothing was installed: the groups were committed (head 0cceb4d1), the version bump was uncommitted and the pre-push full suite was running, because the lane vocabulary has no testing step and the orchestrator set Installing ahead of the real install.
findings.recommendation: Add a bcl job wrapper that records the job pid on the plan group, heartbeats the tracker while the job runs, and writes the lane transition with duration on exit; the page treats a lane with a live recorded job as active instead of Stale.

findings.title: The workflow has no Review stage between Plan & fix and Install
findings.summary: Lane dots already show Fix, Review, Install, Verify, but the workflow definition, top strip, chart, router table and CLI go straight from Plan & fix to Install, so the Terra review and the pre-push suite have no stage of their own.
findings.impact: The page cannot say a group is in review or running its pre-push suite, so labels jump ahead to Installing (see BCL-50).
findings.done_when: workflow_definition.json has a review step (plan_fix, review, install) covering the work-done review (skipped for one-file fixes) and the pre-push suite; the page strip, statechart.html (Current/After, hash), SKILL.md router and bcl CLI all read it from the definition; strict skill-refine passes; named tests prove it on the installed copy.
findings.observed: Guru approved adding the Review stage at 09:49 IST on 18 Nov 2026 after the #115 page showed all lanes Installing during the pre-push suite.
findings.recommendation: Add the step to the definition and derive every view from it; move review text out of plan-fix.md rather than duplicating it.
